title: Pen Plotter Pens, Inks, and Papers Comparison

entries.name: Sakura Pigma Micron
entries.material: Technical pen / Fiber tip (0.15 mm tested)
entries.compatibility: Smooth Bristol paper (chewed up by rough/textured watercolor paper)
entries.notes: Super fine lines; cheap, precise, but fiber nib wears down/degrades quickly on textured paper.

entries.name: Rotring Isograph
entries.compatibility: Cold pressed watercolor paper / Textured paper & Bristol
entries.notes: The 'ultimate pen' for plotters; highly precise, refillable metal nib that survives textured paper; small reservoir (though expandable); permanent ink colors can be slightly dull.

entries.name: Staedtler Permanent Pens
entries.notes: Permanent pigment-based ink, but colors (magenta, cyan, yellow, purple, brown) are noticeably duller than non-permanent dye inks.

entries.name: Stabilo 88
entries.compatibility: Smooth Bristol paper (ruined by textured paper)
entries.lightfastness: No (Not lightfast, colorful inks fade over time)
entries.notes: Great vivid colors, but hexagonal shape makes color alignment slightly annoying; do not sell artwork made with these as they fade.

entries.name: TWSBI Eco
entries.material: Fountain pen / Metal nib (EF, F, M, Stub)
entries.compatibility: Cold pressed watercolor paper / Textured paper
entries.lightfastness: Depends on ink used (Fountain pen inks are generally dye-based & not lightfast)
entries.notes: Plunger mechanism with huge ink capacity; metal nib doesn't wear down on rough/textured paper; Fine or Medium nibs recommended.

entries.name: Brush Pens
entries.notes: Fun expressive line quality; pairs exceptionally well with rough handmade papers.

entries.name: Sakura Gelly Roll (White)
entries.notes: Very difficult to draw clear lines (feels like dusty chalk); temperature dependent (needs warm environment); requires drawing lines twice (forward and back) to show well.

entries.name: Uni-ball UM-120NM
entries.notes: Works better than white gel pens in cold studio environments; metallic silver gives a great high-contrast effect on black paper.

entries.name: Uni-ball Eye (Fine & Micro)
entries.compatibility: Works well on various papers (including textured)
entries.notes: Clear window shows remaining ink level; highly reliable; can leave cap off without drying out easily.

entries.name: Posca Pens
entries.notes: Requires manual repriming/pumping to keep ink flowing during continuous plotting, making long automated runs difficult.

entries.name: Pilot Parallel Pen
entries.notes: Very wide nib capable of unique broad strokes.

entries.name: Faber-Castell Grip-Matic
entries.notes: Presses down to automatically advance lead while drawing up/down strokes; solves mechanical pencil dulling issues on plotters with high pen lifts.

entries.name: Tungsten Engraving Scribe
entries.notes: Used for etching/engraving directly onto copper plates to create traditional prints on plotters.

entries.name: Bristol Paper (Extra Smooth)
entries.notes: Bright white, ultra-smooth surface. Gives clean lines like a laser printer, but fiber tips last longer on it.

entries.name: Cold Pressed Watercolor Paper (Bockingford)
entries.compatibility: Metal nib pens (Fountain pens, Rotring Isograph, Ballpoints)
entries.notes: Textured/rough paper that gives artwork a high-end, classic handmade feel; ruins/chews up fiber-tip pens very quickly.

entries.name: Fabriano Black Paper
entries.compatibility: White gel pens, Metallic pens (Uni-ball silver), Posca pens
entries.notes: Deep black paper ideal for creating high-contrast plots with light or metallic inks.
